entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).
    spaces_filter: Comma-separated list of space keys to filter by.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of simplified Confluence page objects.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_batch_get_changelogs
entries.description:
Get changelogs for multiple Jira issues (Cloud only).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_ids_or_keys: List of issue IDs or keys.
    fields: List of fields to filter changelogs by. None for all fields.
    limit: Maximum changelogs per issue (-1 for all).

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of issues with their changelogs.

Raises:
    NotImplementedError: If run on Jira Server/Data Center.
    ValueError: If Jira client is unavailable.

issue_ids_or_keys.description: Comma-separated list of Jira issue IDs or keys (e.g. 'PROJ-123,PROJ-124')

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to filter changelogs by (e.g. 'status,assignee'). Default to None for all fields.

limit.description: Maximum number of changelogs to return in result for each issue. Default to -1 for all changelogs. Notice that it only limits the results in the response, the function will still fetch all the data.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue
entries.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue including its Epic links and relationship information.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.
    fields: Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'), a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'), '*all' for all fields, or omitted for essentials.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    comment_limit: Maximum number of comments.
    properties: Issue properties to return.
    update_history: Whether to update issue view history.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira issue object.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search
entries.description:
Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    jql: JQL query string.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return.
    limit: Maximum number of results.
    start_at: Starting index for pagination.
    projects_filter: Comma-separated list of project keys to filter by.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    page_token: Pagination token from a previous search result (Cloud only).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the search results including pagination info.

jql.description:
JQL query string (Jira Query Language). Examples:
- Find Epics: "issuetype = Epic AND project = PROJ"
- Find issues in Epic: "parent = PROJ-123"
- Find by status: "status = 'In Progress' AND project = PROJ"
- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"
- Find recently updated: "updated >= -7d AND project = PROJ"
- Find by label: "labels = frontend AND project = PROJ"
- Find by priority: "priority = High AND project = PROJ"

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

projects_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of project keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER if provided.

page_token.description: (Optional) Pagination token from a previous search result. Cloud only — Server/DC uses start_at for pagination.

### Implication for the estimate
Nothing in the frontend knows, or can cheaply learn, which customer group the shopper is in. The three plausible routes all carry server-side dependency:

1. **Extend the existing `c_maxOrderQuantity` hook** to resolve group server-side and emit an already-group-resolved number per SKU. Cheapest frontend (the util and its four call sites already exist), but it depends on TSD-SFCC-268's `afterGET` hook, which per `maxOrderQuantity.ts:19-23` **is still v0.1 Draft, unsigned-off, and not deployed to the dev sandbox**. 3. **Shopper Context `customerGroupIds`** — will not work as a read path (write-only qualifier), and the cache-invalidation side effect is a real cost.

Also note TSD-SFCC-268's documented resolution order (`maxOrderQuantity.ts:34-35`) is **product override → site preference → hardcoded** — customer group is **not** a tier in the already-specified design, so this ticket expands the agreed TSD, it does not just implement it.

### Additional cost the estimate should carry
The PDP and cart are on two separate cap mechanisms, deliberately (`maxOrderQuantity.ts:31-36` documents the duplication as intentional). A group-aware cap that is correct end-to-end has to reconcile both, plus the cart auto-correction path at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useCartMergeAndCap.ts` (188 lines, which reduces over-cap lines on merge) and the drawer guard at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx:326`. # Audit evidence: "PDP — EU Declaration of Conformity PDF Link on Details & Care (EU/EU Int)"

**Headline for the estimate:** the *rendering* half is trivial (one row in an existing presentational component). The *sourcing* half has **zero precedent in this repo** — there is no PDF handling anywhere, no per-product document model in Contentful, no product-type/sunglasses discriminator, and no site allow-list util. Those three gaps are the estimate.

---

## 1. The Details & Care tab component

**File:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/detailsAndCareContent.tsx` (70 lines, whole file read)

### Prop type (lines 8–15, verbatim)

```ts
export type DetailsAndCareContentProps = {
  /** The product's display name — Figma's "Product Description" section heading. */
  displayName: string;
  longDescription?: string;
  /** `c_careInstructions` — same Business-Manager-authored markup shape as `longDescription`. */
  careInstructions?: string;
  styleCode?: string;
};
```

### Sections rendered

| Section | Source | Guard |
|---|---|---|
| Product Description (heading = `displayName`) | SFCC `longDescription` | `!isBlankRichText(longDescription)` — line 52 |
| Care (heading = `<FormattedMessage … id="product_detail.details_and_care.heading.care" />`) | SFCC `c_careInstructions` | `!isBlankRichText(careInstructions)` — line 58 |
| Style Code | SFCC `master.masterId ?? id` via `ZimmProductStyleCode` | renders unconditionally; atom self-nulls — lines 64–67 |

A local `Section` helper (lines 29–36) renders `{heading, body}` with `spacing="var(--zimm-scale-xs)"`; the outer `VStack` uses `spacing="var(--zimm-scale-4xl)"` (line 51).

### Content sourcing — **100% SFCC, zero Contentful**

Docblock lines 38–43 states it explicitly: *"sourced entirely from SFCC attributes via `selectPdpProductInfo` — no Contentful, matching this bucket's confirmed sourcing."* It is **purely presentational** — no hooks other than none at all; react-intl `FormattedMessage` only.

Note lines 17–23: a `material` section was designed (Figma node 40001889:38504) but omitted because *"Tim has confirmed there is no SFCC attribute for it yet (`material = TBD`)"*. **This is the exact same shape of blocker the DoC PDF has today.** Precedent says the repo omits rather than stubs.

### Caller wiring

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1017–1032` — it is tab index 0 in the `pdpDrawerTabs: ZimmPdpDrawerTab[]` array:

```tsx
{
  id: 'details-and-care',
  label: formatMessage({ id: 'product_detail.drawer_trigger.label.details_and_care', defaultMessage: 'Details & Care' }),
  content: (
    <DetailsAndCareContent
      displayName={staticInfo?.name ?? ''}
      longDescription={staticInfo?.description}
      careInstructions={staticInfo?.careInstructions}
      styleCode={staticInfo?.styleCode}
    />
  ),
},
```

`staticInfo` = `selectPdpProductInfo(product, null, product?.currency ?? '', formatPrice)` at `index.tsx:964`.

Also touched by any prop change: `detailsAndCareContent.stories.tsx` (same dir, 2.3 KB) — no `.test.tsx` exists for this partial.

---

## 2. The PDP drawer

**File:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmPdpDrawer/index.tsx` (80 lines)

It **defines no tabs at all**. Line 18–20 comment: *"SFCC-266's EU Environmental Qualities tab, SFCC-102's Size Guide, etc. all pass their own content component here — this organism owns none of it."* It is `ZimmDrawer` (shell) + `ZimmTabs` (nav) + a `tabs.find(t => t.id === activeTabId)` content swap.

```ts
export type ZimmPdpDrawerTab = ZimmTabItem & { content: React.ReactNode };  // line 10-12
```
`ZimmTabItem` = `{ id: string; label: string }` (`../molecules/zimmTabs/index.tsx:8–13`).

Tabs are registered **only** in `product-detail/index.tsx:1017–1080`. Six today: `details-and-care`, `size-guide`, `find-your-size`, `shipping-and-returns`, `assistance`, and conditionally `environmental-qualities`.

The same array feeds the trigger rows (`index.tsx:1321–1326`):
```tsx
<PdpFooterLinks triggers={pdpDrawerTabs.map(({ id, label }) => ({ id, label }))} … />
```

**Verdict: adding a row/link *inside* Details & Care is cheap and non-structural** — a new optional prop on `DetailsAndCareContent` plus one more `<Section>` (or a bare anchor). No drawer, `ZimmTabs`, recipe, or `PdpFooterLinks` change needed. (Adding a *new tab* would also be cheap — the `environmental-qualities` spread at lines 1068–1079 is the template — but the ticket says "inside Details & Care".)

---

## 3. Site/region gating — the mechanism (most important section)

### 3a. Sites and their locales

`config/sites.js` is only a **merge function** (56 lines) over two files. The actual list is `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/config/sites.overlay.js:30–52`:

| PWA site id | `sfccSiteId` | locale | URL alias | EU? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ZimmermannAU` | — | `en` | *(root)* | no |
| `ZimmermannUS` | — | `en-US` | `us` | no |
| `ZimmermannUSIntl` | — | `en-CA` | `en-ca` | no |
| `ZimmermannUK` | — | `en-GB` | `uk` | no |
| **`ZimmermannEUen`** | `ZimmermannEU` | `en-GB` | `en-eu` | **EU domestic** |
| **`ZimmermannEUfr`** | `ZimmermannEU` | `fr` | `fr-eu` | **EU domestic** |
| **`ZimmermannEUit`** | `ZimmermannEU` | `it` | `it-eu` | **EU domestic** |
| **`ZimmermannEUes`** | `ZimmermannEU` | `es` | `es-eu` | **EU domestic** |
| **`ZimmermannEUIntl`** | — | `en-CH` | `en-ch` | **EU International** |
| `ZimmermannHK` | — | `en-HK` | `hk` | no |
| `ZimmermannME` | — | `en-AE` | `en-ae` | no |

**Critical for scoping: "EU + EU Int" is FIVE PWA sites, not two.** EU domestic is four single-locale PWA sites all backed by one SFCC site `ZimmermannEU`; EU International is its own SFCC site `ZimmermannEUIntl`. That means 5 site ids × QA, and **4 non-English locales in scope** (`fr`, `it`, `es` + two English variants).

`config/sites.generated.js` is SCAPI-derived and auto-generated (`npm run sync:regional-config`) — currency/locale truth only; `ZimmermannEU` block at lines ~75–105, `ZimmermannEUIntl` at ~106+.

### 3b. How a component determines the current site — the established pattern

`useMultiSite` ships **untyped** from `@salesforce/retail-react-app`, so every call site does an inline cast. Three real examples:

**Example 1 — the PDP itself already does this** (`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:973–978`):
```ts
const { locale: siteLocale, site } = useMultiSite() as {
  locale?: { id?: string; alias?: string };
  site?: { id?: string };
};
const locale = siteLocale?.id ?? CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE;
const { sizeGuide } = useSizeGuide(staticInfo?.sizeGuide, locale, site?.id ?? '');
```
**`site.id` is already in scope in the PDP container.** A gate costs ~0 additional plumbing there.

**Example 2 — footer, the canonical region-scoping call site** (`overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:194–230`). Lines 194–200 carry the authoritative caveat:
> *"`site.id` here is the correct join key for this lookup specifically: `resolveByRegion.ts` compares it directly against each Contentful `region` entry's `siteId` field, and `seedRegions.mjs`'s `REGION_SEEDS` seeds one entry per PWA site — `ZimmermannEUen/EUfr/EUit/EUes` are each their own entry, never a single shared `'ZimmermannEU'`. **This is a narrower claim than "site.id is generally the resolved SFCC site ID" — it is not, and must not be assumed correct elsewhere by analogy to this lookup.**"*

Resolution at line 230: `pickMostSpecificByRegion<FooterConfigEntry>(configs, site.id)`.

**Example 3 — header nav** (`overrides/app/hooks/useHeaderNav.ts:29, 51, 56`):
```ts
type MultiSiteResult = { site: { id: string }; locale?: { id: string } };
const { site, locale: siteLocale } = useMultiSite() as MultiSiteResult;
// queryKey: [HEADER_NAV_QUERY_KEY, site.id, locale]
```
then `pickMostSpecificByRegion` + `filterByRegion` over items.

**Example 4 (different axis) — `useCountryConfig`** (`overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts:19–23`) matches on `sfccSiteId ?? site.id` **AND** locale, *"to disambiguate the en-GB collision between the UK site and EU English."* This is the trap: `ZimmermannUK` and `ZimmermannEUen` are both `en-GB`. **A locale-based gate would leak the DoC link onto UK.** The gate must be on `site.id`.

### 3c. Is there an existing per-site feature-flag / allow-list util?

**No.** Searched `overrides/app/config/` (5 files: `contentful.ts`, `contentfulMapping.generated.ts`, `contentfulMapping.ts`, `countries.generated.ts`, `countries.ts`) and all 32 files in `overrides/app/utils/`. There is **no** `featureFlags.ts`, no `isFeatureEnabledForSite`, no array-of-site-ids allow-list.

What exists instead — three distinct mechanisms, none of them a feature flag:

1. **`overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts`** — `filterByRegion(entries, siteId)` / `pickMostSpecificByRegion(candidates, siteId)`. Works on any Contentful entry with a `regions: RegionRef[]` field. Empty/omitted `regions` = global fallback, least specific. This is the **only generic gating primitive** and it is *Contentful-entry-shaped* — it cannot gate a hardcoded component.
2. **`overrides/app/config/countries.ts`** — `COUNTRY_OVERLAY` (lines 75–87), a hand-maintained per-slug record of business-logic booleans: `shippingCountry`, `checkoutOwner`, `globalEPricing`, `boutiqueRegion`. **This is the nearest thing to a per-site feature flag in the repo** — `globalEPricing: boolean` is literally a per-site behaviour switch. EU domestic slugs (`en-eu`/`fr-eu`/`it-eu`/`es-eu`) are `checkoutOwner:'sfcc', globalEPricing:false`; `en-ch` is `checkoutOwner:'global-e', globalEPricing:true`. **Note: no single field groups all five EU sites** — `boutiqueRegion: 'europe'` is the only one that does, and it's documented as a boutique-filter key, not a feature gate. Adding a `declarationOfConformity: boolean` field here would be the idiomatic move, but the file has a hard `throw` at lines 101–107 if slugs and overlay drift, and `CountryConfig` is consumed by routing/IP-detection/checkout-redirect/hreflang — a wider blast radius than it looks.
3. **One named site-id constant:** `overrides/app/utils/shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts:10` — `export const EU_DOMESTIC_SFCC_SITE_ID = 'ZimmermannEU';` with a docblock (lines 4–9) explicitly noting this is the shared SFCC id for the four domestic sites and **does not include** `ZimmermannEUIntl`. So even the one EU constant that exists is the wrong shape for this ticket.

### 3d. The closest precedent: how the *existing* EU-only PDP tab is gated

`environmentalQualitiesContent.tsx:11–13` docblock: *"EU storefronts only (en-eu / fr-eu); **the gate lives in product-detail/index.tsx**."*

But the gate is **not** a site check. `index.tsx:966–970`:
```ts
// selectEnvQualitiesContent handles both the locale gate (c_showEnvironmentalNote, resolved
// server-side by the SCAPI hook against request.locale — no PWA locale matching needed) and
// the AP21 → site-pref fallback chain (AC2). Returns undefined when the tab must not appear.
const envQualitiesContent = selectEnvQualitiesContent(staticInfo, isBlankRichText);
```
and `productInfo.ts:221–229`:
```ts
export const selectEnvQualitiesContent = (info, isBlank) => {
  if (info?.showEnvironmentalNote !== true) return undefined;
  …
};
```
with `productInfo.ts:44–47`:
> *"Site preference flag (SFCC-266). The SCAPI hook resolves `showEnvironmentalQualities` against `request.locale` **server-side** and returns the boolean result — true only for EU locales listed in BM. The PWA reads this scalar directly; no locale matching needed."*

**This is the single most important estimate input.** The one EU-only PDP feature already shipped was gated by a **backend-resolved boolean custom attribute (`c_showEnvironmentalNote`) delivered by a SCAPI hook**, not by frontend `site.id` branching. That is the house pattern for exactly this problem — and it required backend/BM work outside this repo. Expect the DoC ticket to want the same (`c_showDeclarationOfConformity` or equivalent), which means a **cross-team dependency, not a FE-only change**.

content.text:
I have everything I need. One confirmatory Confluence lookup (the product-attributes TSD) is still running, but the codebase already answers it directly.

---

# FED estimate audit — SFCC-703, 704, 710

**Headline:** the table's 3 × 2 = 6 FED days sit against **7.5 FED days remaining** of the 20-day enhancement budget (12.5 consumed, per page 385318913). My bottom-up range is **7.0 days (best case) to 11.75 days (worst case)**. The entire swing comes from three unresolved decisions, not from estimating error.

---

## SFCC-703 — Max Purchase Quantity Override by Customer Group and SKU

**Asks for:** merchandiser-set purchase caps at SKU and customer-group level, resolving SKU → group → global default.

**AC quality: YES — 8 testable ACs.** But ACs 1–2 are Business Manager config (BED, not FED), and 3/4/5/7 are resolution-order behaviours the agreed TSD places **server-side**.

### What exists

Your prior investigation is **confirmed for the PDP, refuted for the cart** — there are two independent mechanisms:

| | Mechanism | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **PDP** | Hardcoded | `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:149` — `const MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY = 3;`, used once at `:1330` |
| **Cart** | SFCC-backed | `overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts:51` — `getMaxOrderQuantity()` reads `c_maxOrderQuantity`, falls back to 3. Consumed by `product-item/index.tsx:363`, `useCartMergeAndCap.ts:43`, `cartDrawerContainer.tsx:326` |

So the memory note needs amending: a Salesforce-backed path now exists, just not on the PDP.

Already built: per-SKU aggregation (`product-view/index.tsx:589-597`, keys on `variant.productId`), and both limit-reached messages (`:108-116`), rendered via `ZimmSizeSelector` error state (`:1294-1297`) and inline `Text` (`:939-949`).

**Customer group: zero client-side awareness.** `grep -rniE "customerGroup|groupIds"` excluding `node_modules` returns exactly **one** hit — a GTM dataLayer doc line at `.docs/integration/13-gtm.md:137`. `use-current-customer` is not overridden; base returns only `customerType/customerId/isRegistered/isGuest`. The SDK `Customer` type has no groups field. Shopper Context's `customerGroupIds` is a **write-only qualifier**, not a read path.

**The TSD matters here.** Confluence 406913046 (TSD-SFCC-268) is still **v0.1 Draft, Technical Lead sign-off Pending**, with unfilled `[Name]` placeholders. Its resolution order is *product override → site preference → hardcoded* — **customer group is not a tier in it at all**. It explicitly states SFCC-703's override is "handled at the hook layer with **no PWA changes required**." The ticket as written expands the agreed design.

### FED breakdown

| # | Work | Days |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Wire PDP to real attribute (`getMaxOrderQuantity(product)`; `product` already in scope at `:1330`) | 0.25 |
| 2 | Reconcile the two duplicate constants | 0.25 |
| 3 | Tests for a non-3 cap | 0.5 |
| 4 | Multi-site verification (per-site preference × 8 storefronts) | 0.5 |
| 5a | Customer-group resolution **server-side** (TSD-consistent) | 0 |
| 5b | Customer-group resolution **client-side** — new hook, group→cap match, most-restrictive (AC6), blank fallthrough (AC7) *(speculative — no data source exists)* | +2–3 |

**Bottom-up FED total: 1.5 days (server-side) | 3.5–4.5 days (client-side)**

### Verdict vs table (FED 2 days): ABOUT RIGHT BY ACCIDENT

Delta: **−0.5 d** or **+1.5 to +2.5 d**. Biggest single reason: **the estimate doesn't state who owns customer-group resolution, and that one decision swings FED by 3 days.** BED 2 days also looks light for adding a tier the TSD doesn't have.

### Blockers
- TSD unsigned; its `afterGET` hook **is not deployed** — a live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product (recorded at `maxOrderQuantity.ts:19-23`). The FE has never exercised the real path.
- Jira Dependency field: *"Explore whether multiple customer groups per customer is in scope — if so, recheck AC6"* + *"Depends on SFCC-196."*
- TSD risk row, unresolved: attribute-ID alignment between SFCC-268 and SFCC-703 "before either ticket enters dev."
- **Three-way scope collision:** SFCC-172 (Cart SKU override, To Do, no ACs, `ENH-048`/`CouldHave`) and **SFCC-250** (Cart enforcement, **In Progress, assigned to you**, ACs hardcode "the configured maximum of 3").

### Questions
1. **Victor T. Crisostomo / Tech Lead** — hook-side or frontend customer-group resolution? *This is the estimate.*
2. **Tech Lead** — sign off TSD-SFCC-268 or supersede it; it's the cited source for shipped code.
3. **Jasmijn / BA** — is multi-group membership in scope (AC6)?
4. **Natasha Lay** — SFCC-703 vs 172 vs 250: close SFCC-172 as duplicate?
5. **You** — SFCC-250's ACs bake in "3"; reword before a configurable cap ships?

## SFCC-704 — EU Declaration of Conformity PDF link

**Asks for:** a DoC PDF link inside the PDP Details & Care slide-out, EU + EU-Int only, sunglasses only.

**AC quality: PARTIAL — 5 well-formed ACs, ~2 buildable today.** AC2 contains "TBC with design"; ACs 1/3/5 depend on two data sources that do not exist.

### What it's blocked on — found

Not in comments (there are none). It's in the **Dependency** field (`customfield_10232`), three open items:

1. *"How is the PDF stored and associated to a product — via a product attribute in BM, a DAM, or another asset management system? This determines whether a separate BM configuration story is needed."*
2. *"Confirm with design on PDF display in Details & Care, discuss whether the PDF opens in a new tab or downloads directly."*
3. *"This requirement is currently being implemented on the existing site — confirm whether the approach taken there should be mirrored on the new site."*

To Do → **Blocked** on 2026-09-08 by Jasmijn Tsang.

**Also: the table's "Approved" status is stale.** "PO Approved On" (set 04 Sep) and the "PO approved" Definition-of-Ready checklist item were **both cleared by Hazel Marie Cacalda on 2026-09-14**.

### What exists

- Details & Care component: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/detailsAndCareContent.tsx` — purely presentational, SFCC-sourced. Adding a row = one optional prop + one `<Section>`. Wired at `product-detail/index.tsx:1017-1032`.
- **No PDF handling anywhere** — zero `.pdf`/`application/pdf` matches in `overrides/`, no `<a download>`. One `target="_blank"` precedent: `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:86`.
- **No DoC attribute, no sunglasses discriminator.** The PDP's full custom-attribute set is 18 (verified by grep on `productInfo.ts`): `c_careInstructions, c_color, c_colourId, c_environmentalMessage, c_environmentalNotes, c_fabricComposition, c_hsCode, c_modelFit, c_productBadges, c_relatedSwatches, c_showEnvironmentalNote, c_sizeFit, c_sizeGuide, c_styleId, c_styleNumber, c_stylingNotes, c_tabDescription, c_tabDetails`. - **No site allow-list util exists.** The one shipped EU-only PDP feature (SFCC-266 Environmental Qualities) is gated by a **backend-resolved boolean** `c_showEnvironmentalNote` (`productInfo.ts:44-47`), not frontend `site.id`. That's the house pattern.
- **No Confluence spec page for the DoC exists** — searched, nothing.

**"EU + EU Int" is 5 PWA sites, not 2** — `config/sites.overlay.js:39-44`: `ZimmermannEUen/EUfr/EUit/EUes` (all SFCC `ZimmermannEU`) + `ZimmermannEUIntl`. **Trap:** `ZimmermannUK` and `ZimmermannEUen` are both `en-GB`, so a locale-based gate leaks the link onto UK.

**Translation gap (verified):** `fr.json` 606 keys, `it.json` 597, `es.json` 606 vs `en-GB.json` 817. `extract-default-translations` runs only `en-US en-GB` (`package.json:66`). New react-intl strings render English on `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`. For a **legal compliance link** that is a likely QA rejection.

## SFCC-710 — PDP Wishlist Confirmation Message on Add

**Asks for:** a toast on PDP add-to-wishlist with product name + "View Wishlist" link, auto-dismissing.

**AC quality: YES — 4 testable ACs.** AC2 has "duration TBC". Two gaps: no AC for remove-from-wishlist, and none for the post-login intent replay.

### Is it a duplicate? NO — it's a reversal of a signed-off decision

- Base SFCC **does** toast: `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:266-283` (`global.info.added_to_wishlist` + a "View" action to `/account/wishlist`).
- Zimmermann **kept** it for the set/bundle CTA (`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:532`, toast at `:557`)…
- …and **deliberately removed it for standalone products** — the common case. `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:590-595`, verbatim:

  > `// SFCC-434 — toast-free add, used only by the header wishlist badge on the standalone-product`
  > `// path below. Jasmijn confirmed the PDP badge has no confirmation message, only the icon`
  > `// state change; handleAddToWishlist above keeps its toast for the set/bundle CTA button...`

So SFCC-710 undoes what SFCC-434 (Ready for SIT) built on **Jasmijn's own confirmation** — and Jasmijn is who the table asks to check for duplication. No duplicate ticket exists; the nearest wishlist tickets (SFCC-434, 184, 866, 862, 169, 170) are all distinct.

### What exists — most of it, actually

- `overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts:41-43` already defines `use_cart_messages.added_to_wishlist` = **`'{productName} added to Wishlist'`** — exactly AC1's product-name requirement — exposed as `notifyAddedToWishlist(productName)`. Built for SFCC-272. `notifyAlreadyInWishlist()` too.
- Guest path (AC4) fully built: `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/` + `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` (SFCC-742), with session-persisted intent.
- PDP wishlist button exists (`ZimmWishlistBadge` via `product-view/index.tsx:796`).

**What's missing is the surface, not the logic:**
- **No Zimmermann toast/alert theme recipe** — nothing matching toast/alert under `overrides/app/theme/`. A toast today renders as unbranded base Chakra `<Alert variant="subtle">`.
- `emitCartMessage` passes only `{title, status}` — no action-link support for "View Wishlist".
- `ZimmInlineMessage` exists but is inline-only — no positioning, timer, or action link.
- **SFCC-404 "Cart Message Component - PWA Kit"** (Tech design, **assigned to you**) is the real notification build — but scoped to a cart-drawer banner, with copy from **Contentful UI Copy**, a different mechanism from `useCartMessages`' react-intl. `useCartMessages.ts:108-109` states SFCC-404 replaces the toast renderer.

**Bottom-up FED total: 2.0 days (if SFCC-404 lands first) | 3.0–3.5 days (standalone)**

### Verdict vs table (FED 2 days): NOT A DUPLICATE — but probably shouldn't be built as written

On numbers: **ABOUT RIGHT only if SFCC-404 ships first; otherwise OVER by ~1–1.5 days.** Biggest single reason: **"BED 0 days (using OOTB Wishlist)" is true and irrelevant — the cost was never backend. It's that the frontend has no branded notification surface.**

- Sequencing vs SFCC-404 — build twice or wait.
